newsitem.title: USA: U.S. low sulphur resid still pressured by supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. low sulphur resid still pressured by supply.

text.p: U.S. low sulphur residual fuel remained on the defensive Wednesday in moderate activity, still weighed down by oversupply despite the approach of another Arctic cold wave later this week, sources said.

"It's cold and going to get colder by the weekend, that should chew into inventories, but it just may be a selling opportunity," said one cash trader, noting there was still a lot of oil in tank, particularly of low sulphur grades.
In New York Harbor, traders said 0.3 high pour was driven $1 a barrel lower to $18.75-19.00 on reports NYPA awarded its 100,000-barrel tender for Jan 21-31 delivery at sub-$19.

NYH physical one percent slipped another 25-50 cents to the low-$18 level, pressured by too many barrels on offer. Traders said February paper was off another quarter or so to below $18 despite a sharp rally in crude.
High sulphurs in New York again were unchanged, with 180,000 barrels of fairly prompt 2.2 percent sold late Tuesday at $17.40 (delivered Wilmington, N.C.).

At the U.S. Gulf, one percent skidded 50 cents to $17.25-50. Traders said three percent held relatively steady at about $15.75-16.00 on reports two 40-50,000-barrel pieces were sold late Tuesday at $15.80 and $15.90.
New York city gate swing gas prices jumped more than 60 cents Wednesday to near the $5.00/mmBtu level on the cold. NYH one percent resid was at a $2.88/mmBtu equivalent.
